title_en: Shanghai Chenguang Stationery Co., Ltd. v. Deli Group Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over infringement of design patent
ruling_gist_en: With respect to the determination of similarity in design, the principle of 'overall observation and comprehensive judgment' shall be followed. In specific cases, both the similarity and the differences between the accused infringing design and the authorized design shall be examined; the effects of identical design features and differentiating design features on the overall visual effect shall be objectively analyzed respectively from the perspectives of the accused infringing product and the authorized design, so as to avoid subjective influence. Where a person, without creative effort, practices a design patent by making changes or additions to design elements, patterns, and colors that lack substantive differences on the basis of the authorized design, such conduct constitutes infringement of the design patent right.
keywords_en: civil; dispute over infringement of design patent right; first instance; intermediate people's court; Shanghai; Zhejiang; Shandong; legal person; Patent Law; determination of similarity in design; principle of overall observation and comprehensive judgment; design feature of substantive difference; supporting plaintiff; design patent; gel pen product; manufacturing and selling infringement; patent right; intellectual property; and other disputes over infringement of design patent right
full_text_en:
Shanghai Chenguang Stationery Co., Ltd. v. Deli Group Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over infringement of design patent

Ruling Summary

In determining the similarity of designs, the principle of "overall observation and comprehensive assessment" shall be followed. In specific cases, both the similarities and differences between the accused infringing design and the patented design shall be examined; the impact of the identical design features and the distinguishing design features on the overall visual effect shall be objectively analyzed respectively to avoid subjective influence. Where, without engaging in creative work, a design patent is implemented by altering or adding design elements, patterns, and colors that lack substantive differences on the basis of the patented design, such conduct constitutes infringement of the design patent right.

Plaintiff: Shanghai Chenguang Stationery Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 3469 Jinqian Road, Fengxian District, Shanghai.

Legal Representative: Chen Huwen, Chairman of the Board.

Defendant: Deli Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at Deli Industrial Park, Ninghai County, Ningbo City, Zhejiang Province.

Legal Representative: Lou Fujun, Chairman of the Board.

Defendant: Jinan Kunsen Commercial Trade Co., Ltd., domiciled at Liuzhiyuan Village, Lixia District, Jinan City, Shandong Province.

Legal Representative: Wang Kun.

The plaintiff, Shanghai Chenguang Stationery Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Chenguang"), filed a lawsuit with the Shanghai Intellectual Property Court against the defendants, Deli Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Deli") and Jinan Kunsen Commercial Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Kunsen"), concerning a dispute over infringement of design patent.

Plaintiff's Allegations: On November 26, 2009, the plaintiff filed an application with the China National Intellectual Property Administration (CNIPA) for design patent No. ZL200930231150.3, which was granted and published on July 21, 2010, and remains valid. In November 2015, the plaintiff discovered that the defendant Deli had manufactured and sold the "Deli Sida A32160 Pop Style Neutral Pen," and the defendant Kunsen had also offered for sale and sold the product on the Tmall online marketplace. The plaintiff contends that the product is the same type of product as the plaintiff's patented design and that the designs are similar. The actions of the two defendants constitute infringement of the plaintiff's patent right. The plaintiff requests the court to order: 1. That the two defendants immediately cease infringing the plaintiff's design patent right No. ZL200930231150.3, specifically, that the defendant Deli immediately cease manufacturing and selling, and the defendant Kunsen immediately cease selling and offering for sale; 2. That the two defendants destroy all infringing products in stock as well as the special equipment and molds used for manufacturing the infringing products; 3. That the defendant Deli compensate the plaintiff for economic losses of RMB 1,800,000 and reasonable expenses of RMB 200,000 incurred in stopping the infringement.

Defendant Deli's Defense: Although the accused infringing product was manufactured and sold by the defendant, the product is neither identical nor similar to the patented design of the plaintiff Chenguang, and the defendant's actions do not constitute infringement of the plaintiff's patent right. Even if infringement were established, the amount of damages and reasonable expenses claimed by the plaintiff are excessive. The plaintiff's claims lack factual and legal basis, and the defendant requests the court to dismiss all of the plaintiff's claims.

Defendant Kunsen's Defense: No defense was submitted.

Facts Found by the Shanghai Intellectual Property Court at First Instance:

The plaintiff Chenguang is the holder of the design patent titled "Pen (AGP67101)" under patent number ZL200930231150.3, filed on November 26, 2009, and published on July 21, 2010, which remains valid. The patented design consists of a pen barrel and a cap, with a clip on the cap. The pen barrel is generally a slender, rounded-corner prism of uniform thickness; the top end has a square frustum protrusion with a circular hole in the center; the inner diameter near the nib is slightly smaller; the central positions on each of the four side surfaces have a convex design; the nib is conical. The cap is generally a rounded-corner prism of uniform thickness, with a length approximately one-quarter of the pen barrel; the top end has a square frustum protrusion. The clip is generally a flat rectangular strip; the inner side has a wavy protrusion; the upper end is connected in an arc to the frustum at the top of the cap; the lower end is curved; the clip is slightly longer than the cap, with the extension accounting for about one-tenth of the total length of the clip. The brief explanation of the patent states that the design point lies in the shape of the entire pen, and the top view is the image that best reflects the design point.

On August 14, 2015, the CNIPA, upon the request of the plaintiff Chenguang, issued an evaluation report on the patent in question, concluding preliminarily that "no defects have been found that would prevent the grant of the patent right for the entire design." The report records that 11 prior designs were retrieved based on the design features of the patent in question. After comparison, the patent in question showed significant differences from Design 1 (Chinese design patent publication No. CN3229363) in terms of the shape of the pen barrel, shape of the cap, shape of the clip, and the connection between the cap and the clip; in addition, it was found that "compared with the combination of Design 1-11 and/or the design features of Design 1-11, this patent does not exhibit a lack of distinctiveness."

On March 18, 2016, the defendant Deli filed a request for invalidation of the patent in question with the Patent Reexamination Board of the CNIPA, arguing that the patent in question was similar to the design disclosed in Chinese design patent publication No. CN300885158 and thus did not meet the conditions for grant of patent right. On August 8, 2016, the Patent Reexamination Board issued a decision, holding that the patented design and the cited design did not constitute substantial similarity, and maintained the validity of the patent in question.

On November 30, 2015, a search for "Deli A32160" on the "Products" tab of Taobao.com displayed "7 products in total," with prices ranging from RMB 1.0 per pen to RMB 26.90 per box (12 pens). The agent ad litem of the Shanghai Branch of Beijing King & Wood Mallesons Law Firm purchased four boxes of Deli Sida A32160 Pop Style Neutral Pens from the "Deli Kunsen Specialized Store," priced at RMB 26.90 per box. The "Deli Kunsen Specialized Store" is operated by the defendant Kunsen. The defendant Deli confirmed that it had manufactured and sold the accused infringing products.

The accused infringing product consists of a pen barrel and a cap, with a clip on the cap. The pen barrel is generally a rounded-corner prism of uniform thickness, with a ring-shaped groove design approximately one-third of the barrel length from the nib; the top end has a square frustum protrusion with a circular hole in the center; the inner diameter near the nib is slightly smaller; the central positions on each of the four side surfaces have a convex design; the nib is conical. The cap is generally a rounded-corner prism of uniform thickness, with a length approximately one-quarter of the pen barrel; the top end has a square frustum protrusion. The clip is generally rectangular; the outer side has a rectangular frustum protrusion, while the inner side is smooth; the upper end of the clip is connected in an arc to the frustum at the top of the cap; the lower end is straight; the clip is slightly longer than the cap, with the extension accounting for about one-tenth of the total length of the clip.

Upon comparison (see accompanying drawings), the accused infringing design and the patented design are substantially identical in terms of basic composition, overall shape of the pen barrel and cap, shape of the top ends of the pen barrel and cap, the length of the cap relative to the pen barrel, the connection between the clip and the cap, and the length by which the clip extends beyond the cap. Specifically: 1. Both consist of a pen barrel and a cap, with a clip on the cap; 2. The pen barrel and cap are both generally rounded-corner prisms of uniform thickness; 3. The top ends of both the pen barrel and the cap have a square frustum protrusion, with a circular hole in the center of the frustum on the pen barrel; 4. The length of the cap is approximately one-quarter of the length of the pen barrel; 5. The upper end of the clip is connected in an arc to the frustum at the top of the cap; 6. The clip is slightly longer than the cap, with the extension accounting for about one-tenth of the total length of the clip; 7. The inner diameter near the nib is slightly smaller, and the central positions on each of the four side surfaces have a convex design, with the nib being conical. The main differences are: 1. The accused infringing design has a ring-shaped groove design approximately one-third of the barrel length from the nib, whereas the patented design does not; 2. The outer side of the clip in the accused infringing design has a rectangular frustum protrusion, whereas the outer side of the clip in the patented design has no such protrusion; 3. The inner side of the clip in the accused infringing design is smooth, whereas the inner side of the clip in the patented design has a wavy protrusion; 4. The lower end of the clip in the accused infringing design is straight, whereas the lower end of the clip in the patented design is curved.

Additionally, it was found that the plaintiff Chenguang incurred legal fees of RMB 200,000 for this case.

Regarding the disputed issue of the defendant Deli's profit from infringing activities, the plaintiff Chenguang submitted the following evidence: the article "Deli Group Internet Case Study" from the National Transportation Logistics Public Information Platform; the article "'IPO Wave' Hits: Overview of Listed Stationery Industry Giants" from Century Stationery Network; relevant product category pages from Deli's official website; the plaintiff's 2015 annual report; the sales page for Deli A32160 neutral pens on the "Huabin Stationery" online store on alibaba.com; and the plaintiff's cost accounting table for the patented product. This evidence was intended to show that the defendant Deli had made substantial profits from manufacturing and selling the accused infringing product. The plaintiff provided two calculation methods: First, according to the article "'IPO Wave' Hits: Overview of Listed Stationery Industry Giants," Chenguang's net profit margin in 2013 was 11.7%, and True Color Stationery's was 3.89%, yielding an average profit margin for stationery products of 7.79%. The article "Deli Group Internet Case Study" stated that Deli's sales exceeded 60 billion yuan in 2013; Deli's official website listed a total of 4,390 products. From this, the sales revenue per product could be derived, and using the above average profit margin, the average annual profit per product would be RMB 10.6 million. Second, the wholesale price of the accused infringing product on the "Huabin Stationery" online store was RMB 1.06 per pen, and the direct cost for the plaintiff to produce the patented product was RMB 0.5051 per pen, yielding a profit margin of 52.35% for the accused infringing product. The plaintiff's total output of writing instruments in 2015 was 1.87 billion pens, across 1,100 models, so the annual output per model was 1.7 million pens. Since Deli is similar in scale to the plaintiff, the annual output of the accused infringing product could be presumed to be 1.7 million pens. Based on the above wholesale price, annual output, and profit margin, the annual profit of the accused infringing product would be RMB 940,000, and Deli's total profit over two years would be RMB 1.88 million. The defendant Deli challenged the authenticity and relevance of the above evidence and argued that the calculation methods lacked reasonableness. The defendant Deli submitted a statistical table on the sales and profit of the accused infringing product, claiming that the product was launched on April 10, 2014, and the last shipment from headquarters occurred in October and November 2014; Deli's profit from manufacturing and selling the accused infringing product was only RMB 3,677.24. The plaintiff challenged the authenticity of this statistical data.

The court made the following findings regarding the disputed facts: Neither of the two calculation methods provided by the plaintiff Chenguang could prove the profit of the defendant Deli. For the first method, first, the content on Deli's official website indicated that Deli's products include printers, paper, safes, and many other products, not just pens. The unit prices of various products vary greatly, and sales volumes also differ. Calculating the sales amount of the accused infringing product by dividing the total sales amount of all Deli products by the number of product categories is clearly lacking in objectivity and reasonableness. Second, the sampling for the average profit margin should be broad; using only the profit margins of two companies as a basis to calculate the industry average profit margin is not objective. Third, even under the plaintiff's calculation method, the annual profit per product was only slightly over RMB 100,000, not RMB 10.6 million, and that profit was not profit from infringement. For the second method, first, in the first method, the plaintiff claimed that True Color's profit margin was 3.89% and Chenguang's was 11.7%; in the second method, the plaintiff claimed a profit margin of 52.35% for the accused infringing product. The figures vary widely, making it difficult to accept the claimed profit margin. Second, according to common experience, the output of different enterprises varies, and the output of different models within the same enterprise also varies. The plaintiff did not directly provide the output of its patented product but calculated the output of the patented product based on the total output of all its writing instruments and the number of product models, and then inferred the output of the accused infringing product. This lacks objectivity and reasonableness. Therefore, neither of the two calculation methods provided by the plaintiff can prove Deli's profits. As for the profit amount claimed by Deli, since it was self-reported by Deli without other evidence corroborating its authenticity, it is also not credited. In summary, the above evidence and the profit amounts claimed by both parties based on it are not credited.

Opinion of the Court at First Instance:

I. The accused infringing design falls within the scope of protection of the plaintiff Chenguang's design patent, and the actions of the two defendants, Deli and Kunsen, constitute infringement of the plaintiff's design patent right.

In this case, both the accused infringing product and the plaintiff's patented product are pens, i.e., products of the same category. There are certain differences in the overall visual effect between the two, so the designs are not identical. The main dispute in the case is whether the accused infringing design and the patented design are similar, i.e., whether there is a substantial difference in overall visual effect. In making this determination, the principle of overall observation and comprehensive assessment should be applied, considering both the similarities and differences. The same design features and distinguishing design features of the accused infringing design and the patented design should be examined respectively to assess their impact on the overall visual effect.

As for the same design features, the design features of the patented design, such as the shape of the pen barrel body, the shape of the top end of the pen barrel, the shape of the cap body, the shape of the top end of the cap, the length of the cap relative to the pen barrel, the connection between the clip and the cap, and the length by which the clip extends beyond the cap, collectively determine the design style of the patented design. Since these features are all present in the accused infringing design, it can be concluded that the two are similar in overall design style and main design features.

Regarding the impact of the distinguishing features on the overall visual effect, the court holds: 1. The smooth design of the inner side of the clip is a conventional design and is located in a part not easily observed by ordinary consumers, thus having a very limited impact on the overall visual effect; 2. The difference in the curved lower end of the clip is only a minor local difference in the pen as a whole, insufficient to affect the overall visual effect; 3. Although the rectangular frustum protrusion on the outer side of the clip occupies a relatively large area on the clip, the impact of the clip on the overall visual effect of the pen is primarily determined by its overall shape, size, connection to the cap, and the length of its extension beyond the cap. Since these factors are the same, the frustum protrusion on the outer side of the clip has a limited impact on the overall visual effect and is insufficient to constitute a substantial difference; 4. The ring-shaped groove design on the pen barrel is located approximately one-third of the barrel length from the nib, only encircling the barrel transversely, with a small area. It is a local design feature and has a limited impact on the overall visual effect. In summary, the four distinguishing design features between the accused infringing design and the patented design are insufficient to constitute a substantial difference in overall visual effect.

The defendant Deli argued that the accused infringing design adopted colors and patterns different from those of the patented design, and that such colors and patterns would have a significant impact on the overall visual effect, thus the designs are not similar. In this regard, the court holds that the scope of protection of a design patent is determined by the design of the product as shown in the drawings or photographs. Shape, pattern, and color are three basic design elements constituting a product's design. According to Article 28 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, if a design claims protection for color, it must be stated in the brief explanation. The brief explanation of the patented design in this case does not explicitly claim protection for color; therefore, when determining the scope of protection and making an infringement determination, color should not be taken into account. Furthermore, as seen from the drawings or photographs showing the patented design, there is no pattern formed by changes in light and shade or depth arising from the shape; therefore, the pattern element should not be considered in the infringement determination either. The colors, patterns, and other elements added by the accused infringing design while adopting a shape similar to the patented design are additional design elements that do not have a substantive impact on the infringement determination. Otherwise, others could easily circumvent patent infringement by simply adding patterns, colors, or the like to a patented design, which would undoubtedly contradict the legislative intent of the Patent Law, which encourages inventions and innovations and promotes scientific and technological progress. Therefore, the opinion of the defendant Deli is not accepted.

In summary, the accused infringing design adopts a design style similar to the patented design and uses design features that affect the overall visual effect of the patented design. The differences between the two are insufficient to have a substantive impact on the overall visual effect, i.e., they do not constitute a substantial difference. Therefore, the accused infringing design is similar to the patented design and falls within the scope of protection of the plaintiff Chenguang's design patent right. The manufacturing and selling of the accused infringing product by the defendant Deli without the plaintiff's permission, and the selling and offering for sale by the defendant Kunsen, constitute infringement of the plaintiff's design patent right.

II. Both defendants, Deli and Kunsen, shall bear the civil liability to cease infringement, and the defendant Deli shall additionally bear the civil liability to compensate for losses.

In this case, both the plaintiff Chenguang and the defendant Deli are relatively influential stationery manufacturers in China and should invest more effort in independent research and development of new products and have a relatively professional understanding of the legal risks involved in their own product development. The defendant Deli, without engaging in creative work, implemented the plaintiff's design patent by altering or adding design elements, patterns, and colors that lack substantive differences on the basis of the plaintiff's patented design, thereby infringing the plaintiff's design patent right. The defendant Kunsen, by selling and offering for sale the accused infringing product, also infringed the plaintiff's design patent right. Both defendants shall bear corresponding civil liability.

Regarding the plaintiff Chenguang's request for the court to order the two defendants, Deli and Kunsen, to destroy infringing products in stock and the special equipment and molds used for manufacturing the infringing products, the court holds that the plaintiff has not submitted evidence proving that the two defendants have any stock or that they possess special equipment and molds for manufacturing the infringing products. Since ordering the defendants to cease infringement is sufficient to prevent future infringement, the plaintiff's request in this regard is not supported.

For the amount of damages, the plaintiff, Chenguang Company, claimed that the defendant, Deli Company, had made an infringing profit of over RMB 1.8 million and should be ordered to pay damages in that amount; if Deli’s profit was difficult to ascertain, statutory damages should apply. The defendant, Deli Company, argued that its infringing profit could be determined, amounting to RMB 3,677.24, and that damages should be calculated based on that profit, without resorting to statutory damages. In response, the court held that although the plaintiff requested damages to be calculated on the basis of Deli’s infringing profit, the evidence submitted by the plaintiff was insufficient to constitute prima facie evidence of Deli’s profit. Furthermore, Deli’s calculation of sales costs and profits was not corroborated by other evidence, and its authenticity and objectivity could not be confirmed; therefore, it could not be accepted. Under these circumstances, the court may, in accordance with legal provisions and the plaintiff’s request, apply statutory damages and determine the amount of compensation by considering factors such as the type of patent right, the nature and circumstances of the infringement. Taking into account the specific circumstances of this case, the court mainly considered the following factors: 1. The plaintiff’s patent is a design patent; 2. The patent term began on November 26, 2009, and at the time of the infringement, the period of protection was nearly half expired; 3. The profit margin for pen products is limited; 4. When consumers choose pen products, in addition to shape, factors such as brand, refill quality, appearance pattern, and color are also primary considerations. That is, the profit obtained by Deli from using the licensed design shape constitutes only part of the profit from the accused infringing product, and the entire profit from the accused infringing product cannot be taken as the infringing profit in this case. Based on the above factors and other circumstances of this case, the court determined that the defendant, Deli Company, shall compensate the plaintiff for economic losses in the amount of RMB 50,000.

Regarding the reasonable expenses incurred by the plaintiff, Chenguang Company, in stopping the infringement, the plaintiff specified at trial that the attorney’s fee was RMB 200,000. The court held that, in accordance with the provisions of Article 65 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, the amount of damages shall include the reasonable expenses paid by the patentee to stop the infringement. The plaintiff did engage an attorney to conduct the lawsuit and paid RMB 200,000 in legal service fees. The court respects the efforts made by all litigation participants, including attorneys, in clarifying the facts and allocating responsibilities in this case. The attorney’s fee is a matter of party autonomy between the parties and the attorney, and the court does not interfere. However, the expenses that the law requires the infringer to bear as the patentee’s costs should be limited to a reasonable range; amounts exceeding a reasonable range should not be borne by the infringer. Therefore, taking into account the complexity of this case, the attorney's workload, the actual amount of damages awarded compared to the amount sought, and with reference to the attorney fee standards prescribed by the judicial administrative department, the court determined that the defendant, Deli Company, shall pay the plaintiff RMB 50,000 in attorney’s fees.

In conclusion, the Shanghai Intellectual Property Court, in accordance with Article 118 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, paragraphs 2 of Articles 11 and 65 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 144 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 241 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on December 12, 2016:

1. The defendant, Deli Group Co., Ltd., shall immediately cease manufacturing and selling products that infringe the design patent right of the plaintiff, Shanghai Chenguang Stationery Co., Ltd., under Patent No. ZL200930231150.3, effective from the date this judgment takes effect;

2. The defendant, Jinan Kunsen Commercial and Trading Co., Ltd., shall immediately cease offering for sale and selling products that infringe the design patent right of the plaintiff, Shanghai Chenguang Stationery Co., Ltd., under Patent No. ZL200930231150.3, effective from the date this judgment takes effect;

3. The defendant, Deli Group Co., Ltd., shall, within ten days from the date this judgment takes effect, compensate the plaintiff, Shanghai Chenguang Stationery Co., Ltd., for economic losses in the amount of RMB 50,000 and reasonable expenses for stopping the infringement in the amount of RMB 50,000;

4. The remaining claims of the plaintiff, Shanghai Chenguang Stationery Co., Ltd., are dismissed.

After the first-instance judgment, neither the plaintiff nor the defendants appealed, and the judgment has become legally effective.
